formula: sales ~ pop + price + (1 | state) + (1 | year)
notes: plm 2.6-7 ranef.plm.Rd example: tw <- plm(sales ~ pop + price, data = Cigar, model = random, effect = twoways), then ranef(tw) and ranef(tw, effect = time): the two-ways error-components model, crossed state and year intercepts (46 states 1963-1992, Baltagi's cigarette demand panel). state is an integer code, year 63-92. pop16, cpi, ndi and pimin are unused columns. Same data as rabe_hesketh cigar.dta, fitted there with another specification.

formula: lcrmrte ~ lprbarr + lpolpc + lprbconv + lprbpris + lavgsen + ldensity + lwcon + lwtuc + lwtrd + lwfir + lwser + lwmfg + lwfed + lwsta + lwloc + lpctymle + lpctmin + region + smsa + factor(year) + (1 | county)
notes: plm vignettes A_plmPackage (Instrumental variable estimators) and B_plmFunction: cr <- plm(lcrmrte ~ lprbarr + lpolpc + lprbconv + lprbpris + lavgsen + ldensity + lwcon + ... + lpctmin + region + smsa + factor(year) | . - lprbarr - lpolpc + ltaxpc + lmix, data = Crime, model = random), Baltagi (2005, 2013, 2021) tables 7.1 and 7.3 (EC2SLS, G2SLS): a county random-intercept model (90 North Carolina counties 1981-1987) in which lprbarr and lpolpc are instrumented by ltaxpc and lmix. The instrumenting is not representable, so the formula renders the error-components regression and the instruments ltaxpc and lmix stay unlisted. The help page says the precomputed l* logs must be used to reproduce the literature, so the response is the column lcrmrte and the raw levels are ignored. Same data as rabe_hesketh crime.dta.

formula: log(emp) ~ log(wage) + log(capital) + (1 | firm)
notes: plm fits EmplUK (Arellano and Bond 1991, 140 UK firms 1976-1984, unbalanced) only by dynamic panel GMM (pgmm.Rd: log(emp) ~ lag(log(emp), 1:2) + lag(log(wage), 0:1) + log(capital) + lag(log(output), 0:1), effect = twoways), by FGLS pooling and within (A_plmPackage: pggls(log(emp) ~ log(wage) + log(capital), data = EmplUK, model = pooling / within)) and in serial-correlation tests; no random-effects fit. Per this pass's panel ruling the firm is rendered as a random intercept on the pggls specification; the lags are not representable. sector and output are unused columns; year is the panel time index.

formula: lgaspcar ~ lincomep + lrpmg + lcarpcap + (1 | country)
notes: plm phtest.Rd example: form <- lgaspcar ~ lincomep + lrpmg + lcarpcap; re <- plm(form, data = Gasoline, model = random), compared with the within fit by the Hausman test (Baltagi and Griffin 1983, 18 OECD countries 1960-1978). All four columns are logs as documented. phtest(form, data = Gasoline, effect = time) also fits a year-effects model inside the test, not filed as a row. year is the panel time index. Not the nlme Gasoline table.

formula: inv ~ value + capital + (1 | firm)
notes: plm vignette A_plmPackage: grun.re <- plm(inv~value+capital, data = Grunfeld, model = random), the one-way error-components model on firm (10 firms 1935-1954, Baltagi 2001's version); B_plmFunction reproduces Baltagi (2013, 2021) table 2.1 with the Wallace-Hussain, Amemiya and Swamy-Arora variance estimators of the same model. pvcm(inv~value+capital, data = Grunfeld, model = random) fits Swamy random coefficients on value and capital per firm, the same grouping, not a further row. Row 2 is the two-ways model; year is the time index in this row.

formula: inv ~ value + capital + (1 | firm) + (1 | year)
notes: plm vignette A_plmPackage: grun.tways <- plm(inv~value+capital, data = Grunfeld, effect = twoways, model = random, random.method = amemiya); B_plmFunction reproduces Baltagi (2013) pp. 51-53, tables 3.1-3.3 with Wallace-Hussain, Swamy-Arora and Amemiya: crossed firm and year intercepts (the year variance is estimated negative and set to 0 by the first two).

formula: mv ~ crim + zn + indus + chas + nox + rm + age + dis + rad + tax + ptratio + blacks + lstat + (1 | townid)
notes: plm vignette A_plmPackage (Unbalanced panels): Hed <- plm(mv~crim+zn+indus+chas+nox+rm+age+dis+rad+tax+ptratio+blacks+lstat, data = Hedonic, model = random, index = townid), Harrison and Rubinfeld (1978) as reproduced in Baltagi and Chang (1994) table 2 and Baltagi (2013) tables 9.1 and 9.3; B_plmFunction repeats it with Stata's and EViews' variance estimators. 506 Boston census tracts in 92 towns with a town random intercept. As the first rows show, mv is the log median value and several regressors are stored transformed (rm and nox squared, dis, rad and lstat logged), as in Baltagi's file.

formula: lnhr ~ lnwg + (1 | id)
notes: No plm example fits LaborSupply; the help page cites Cameron and Trivedi (2005) and Ziliak (1997). The book's program mma21p1panfeandre.do (cameron.econ.ucdavis.edu/mmabook, section 21.3.1-3, Table 21.2) fits pooled OLS, between, within, first differences and random effects by xtreg lnhr lnwg, re i(id) and xtreg lnhr lnwg, mle i(id) on MOM.dat, the JBES posting of these data (532 men 1979-1988; the first rows equal camerondata laborpanel). kids, age and disab are optional extra regressors of that program, left out of the reported model. year is the panel time index.

formula: wage ~ school + exper + I(exper^2) + union + married + ethn + (1 | nr)
notes: No plm example fits Males; the help page cites Vella and Verbeek (1998) and Verbeek (2004, A Guide to Modern Econometrics). Recalled from Verbeek section 10.3 (Illustration: explaining individual wages, Table 10.2), not checked: the log wage equation for these 545 men 1980-1987 by between, fixed effects, OLS and random effects (GLS) on schooling, experience and its square, union, married, black and hispanic and a public-sector dummy, which here is a level of industry and is left out. wage is the log hourly wage. health, industry, occupation and residence are unused columns; year is the panel time index. Same data as wooldridge wagepan.

formula: ls ~ ld + (1 | country)
notes: No plm example fits Parity. The cited Coakley, Fuertes and Smith (2006) test purchasing power parity by regressing the log spot rate on the log price differential with country-specific coefficients (recalled, not read); rendered per this pass's panel ruling with a country random intercept (17 OECD countries, 104 quarters 1973Q1-1998Q4). lp, is, il, uis and uil serve the other parity relations and are unused here; time is the quarter index.

formula: log(gsp) ~ log(pcap) + log(pc) + log(emp) + unemp + (1 | state)
notes: plm vignette B_plmFunction: PrSwar <- plm(log(gsp) ~ log(pcap) + log(pc) + log(emp) + unemp, Produc, model = random, random.method = swar, random.dfcor = 3), Munnell (1990) public capital productivity, 48 states 1970-1986 (Baltagi 2013). Row 2 adds year effects, row 3 nests states in regions with another regressor set. hwy, water and util are the components of pcap and unused here; year is the panel time index.

formula: log(gsp) ~ log(pcap) + log(pc) + log(emp) + unemp + (1 | state) + (1 | year)
notes: plm vignette B_plmFunction (The twoways effect model): Prw <- plm(log(gsp) ~ log(pcap) + log(pc) + log(emp) + unemp, Produc, model = random, random.method = walhus, effect = twoways, random.dfcor = 3), updated to Swamy-Arora and Amemiya, EViews' output in Baltagi (2009) pp. 60-62: crossed state and year intercepts.

formula: log(gsp) ~ log(pc) + log(emp) + log(hwy) + log(water) + log(util) + unemp + (1 | region) + (1 | state)
notes: plm vignette B_plmFunction (Nested error component model): swar <- plm(log(gsp) ~ log(pc) + log(emp) + log(hwy) + log(water) + log(util) + unemp, Produc, index = c(state, year, region), model = random, effect = nested, random.method = swar), replicating Baltagi, Song and Jung (2001) table 6 and Baltagi (2021) table 9.1: a region effect and a state-within-region effect. region holds the 9 census regions; pcap is the sum of hwy, water and util, which enter separately here.

formula: log(goutput) ~ log(seed) + log(totlabor) + log(size) + (1 | id)
notes: plm piest.Rd and aneweytest.Rd: piest(log(goutput) ~ log(seed) + log(totlabor) + log(size), RiceFarms, index = id), Chamberlain's pi-matrix estimator and the Angrist-Newey test of correlated effects, no random-effects fit; Feng and Horrace (2012) fit stochastic frontiers with farm effects. Per this pass's panel ruling the farm (171 Indonesian farms, 6 seasons each) is rendered as a random intercept on the piest specification. goutput is gross rice output in kg; noutput (net of harvest cost) is the alternate response. region (6 villages), status, varieties, bimas and the other input and price columns are unused.

formula: n ~ w + k + (1 | firm)
notes: No plm example fits Snmesp. The cited Alonso-Borrego and Arellano (1999, JBES) estimate dynamic employment and wage equations for these 738 Spanish firms 1983-1990 by symmetrically normalized GMM (abstract read, equations not); rendered per this pass's panel ruling with a firm random intercept on log employment n, with log wages w and log capital k as in plm's employment equation for EmplUK, which are the reader's choice of regressors; the lags are not representable. y, i and f are unused columns; year is the panel time index.

formula: log(gdp) ~ sr + opec + com + (1 | country)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: no plm example fits SumHes and the help page names no model; the cited Hayashi (2000) uses the table in the chapter 5 empirical exercise (pp. 358-363, not read). Penn World Table 5, 125 countries 1960-1985; log real GDP per capita on the saving rate and the OPEC and communist-regime indicators with a country random intercept is the reader's proposal. pop is an unused column; year is the panel time index.

formula: log(earnings/hours) ~ educatn + (1 | intnum)
notes: Cameron and Trivedi (2005) section 9.2; the book's program mma09p1np.do drops zero earnings, keeps women aged 36 with known education and estimates the density of lnhwage = ln(earnings/hours) and its lowess regression on educatn (Figures 9.1-9.3), nonparametric and without grouping. A 1993 PSID cross-section of 4856 women despite the name: intnum is the 1968 family interview number, so women of one PSID family share it (persnum numbers persons within it), rendered as a family random intercept per the repeating-cluster ruling. The book's subset is earnings > 0 and age == 36; hours is the wage's denominator; sex is constant (all women); kids counts births, which the program says not to use.

formula: lnhr ~ lnwg + (1 | id)
notes: Cameron and Trivedi (2005) section 21.3; the book's program mma21p1panfeandre.do (Table 21.2, pp. 709-14) fits pooled OLS, between, within, first differences and random effects by xtreg lnhr lnwg, re i(id) (GLS) and xtreg lnhr lnwg, mle i(id) on these data (MOM.dat, Ziliak 1997: 532 men 1979-1988). kids, ageh and disab are optional extra regressors left out of the reported model; agesq is ageh squared; year is the panel time index. Same data as plm LaborSupply.

formula: lnhr ~ lnwg + kids + ageh + I(ageh^2) + disab + (1 | id)
notes: Cameron and Trivedi (2005) section 22.3; the book's program mma22p1pangmm.do (Table 22.2, pp. 754-6) first-differences the model and fits pooled OLS, 2SLS and two-step GMM of dlnhr on dlnwg dkids dageh dagesq ddisab with lagged instruments (Ziliak 1997), no random-effects fit; rendered per this pass's panel ruling with a person random intercept. The same data as laborpanel at seven decimals (MOMprecise.dat), on whose rounded copy chapter 21 fits xtreg lnhr lnwg, re. agesq is ageh squared; year is the panel time index.

formula: mdvis ~ logc + idp + lpi + fmde + physlm + disea + hlthg + hlthf + hlthp + linc + lfam + educdec + xage + female + child + fchild + black + (1 | zper)
notes: Cameron and Trivedi (2005) section 20.3; the book's program mma20p1count.do (pp. 671-4) uses all study years (unlike chapter 16) and fits poisson and nbreg of MDU (mdvis) on these 17 regressors (Deb and Trivedi 2002), with standard errors clustered on zper, no random-effects fit; the person (zper, up to 5 years each) is rendered as a random intercept per this pass's panel ruling. NB2 is also fitted; the family stays on the count rule since Poisson comes first. Row 2 is the chapter 16 expenditure model. The other expenditure and visit columns are alternate responses; coins, income, num, lnum, pioff and mdeoff are the raw or duplicate forms of logc, linc, lfam, lpi and fmde; xghindx is the imputed ghindx; plan, site, tookphys, time, mhi and ghindx are unused; year is the study year.

formula: lnmeddol ~ logc + idp + lpi + fmde + physlm + disea + hlthg + hlthf + hlthp + linc + lfam + educdec + xage + female + child + fchild + black + (1 | zper)
notes: Cameron and Trivedi (2005) section 16.6; the book's program mma16p3selection.do (pp. 553-5) keeps year == 2 only and fits a two-part model (probit of binexp, then regress of LNMED = lnmeddol on the same 17 regressors for positive expenditure) and Heckman selection models; this row is the second part, on the whole table with the person random intercept per the panel ruling, the book's subset (year == 2, meddol > 0) named here. lnmeddol is missing where meddol is 0; binexp (the first part's indicator) and meddol are alternate forms of the response.

formula: lnexp12m ~ lnhhexp + age + sex + hhsize + farm + educ + (1 | commune)
notes: Cameron and Trivedi (2005) section 24.7 (Table 24.4, pp. 848-53); the book's program mma24p1olscluster.do fits regress LNEXP12M LNHHEXP AGE SEX HHSIZE FARM EDUC with cluster(COMMUNE), then xtreg on the commune with re (FGLS) and mle, plus fe and pa (Vietnam Living Standards Survey 1997-98, 194 communes). lnexp12m is log household health expenditure, missing for households without any (the book's N is 5006).

formula: pharvis ~ lnhhexp + insurance + sex + age + married + illdays + actdays + injury + illness + educ + (1 | commune)
notes: Cameron and Trivedi (2005) section 24.7 (Tables 24.5-24.6; the help's section field is blank); the book's program mma24p2poiscluster.do fits poisson PHARVIS on these regressors with cluster(COMMUNE), then xtpois PHARVIS ..., re i(COMMUNE) and fe. RULE GAP: Stata's xtpoisson re puts a gamma-distributed multiplicative effect on the commune; the formula renders it as a Gaussian random intercept on the log scale. age holds values near 3-4, apparently log years though the page says years.

formula: lowbrth ~ d90 + afdcprc + I(afdcprc^2) + lphypc + lbedspc + lpcinc + lpopul + (1 | state)
notes: Not used in the text of the help's edition; its notes say that afdcprc and its square give interesting findings for pooled OLS and fixed effects (first differencing) on these two years (1987, 1990) of 50 states. The other regressors are recalled from a later-edition computer exercise (lowbrth on d90, afdcprc, lphypc, lbedspc, lpcinc and lpopul by pooled OLS, then first differences), not checked; rendered per this pass's panel ruling with a state random intercept. infmort is the alternate response; stateabb aliases state and year aliases d90; the c* columns are first differences and afdcpsq the square; pcinc, physicpc, bedspc and popul are the raw forms of the logged regressors.

formula: math4 ~ lrexpp + lrexpp_1 + lenrol + lunch + factor(year) + (1 | distid)
notes: Wooldridge pages 479-480 and 505-506 use these Michigan district panels (Papke) in computer exercises; recalled, not checked: math4 on year dummies, log real spending per pupil and its lag, log enrollment and lunch, by first differences and fixed effects, no random-effects fit. Rendered per this pass's panel ruling with a district random intercept (550 districts, 1992-1998; 1992 has no lagged spending). intid, the intermediate school district that nests the districts, is not fitted. math7, drop and grad are alternate outcomes; the y* dummies code year; the other l*, g*, c*, *_1, *sq and *92 columns are transforms of spending, the foundation grant, enrollment, lunch and math4.

formula: math4 ~ lexppp + lunch + (1 | dcode)
notes: The help's notes: a simple regression of math4 on lexppp gives a negative coefficient and controlling for lunch makes the spending coefficient positive (Wooldridge page 18), OLS on Michigan elementary schools (bcode, one row each) in 2001. Schools repeat within districts (dcode), rendered as a district random intercept per the repeating-cluster ruling though the source treats schools as independent. read4 is the alternate response; expend, exppp and lexpend are other forms of spending; lenroll is log(enroll), which is unused.

formula: math4 ~ pctsgle + lmedinc + free + (1 | dcode)
notes: Wooldridge (6th edition) pages 100, 145-146 and 198 use these 229 Michigan schools in computer exercises; recalled, not checked: math4 on pctsgle (percent of children in the school's zipcode not in married-couple families), then adding lmedinc and free, by OLS. Schools repeat within districts (dcode), rendered as a district random intercept per the repeating-cluster ruling; zipcode, the unit of the census columns (medinc, totchild, married, single, pctsgle), also repeats and is left out. read4 is the alternate response; lunch is free + reduced; lenroll and lexppp are logs of enroll and exppp.

formula: mrdrte ~ exec + unem + factor(year) + (1 | id)
notes: Wooldridge pages 480, 505 and 548 use this state panel (1987, 1990, 1993) in computer exercises; recalled, not checked: mrdrte on year dummies, exec and unem by pooled OLS and first differences, then fixed effects and an IV version, no random-effects fit; rendered per this pass's panel ruling with a state random intercept on id. state is the postal code of id; d90 and d93 code year; the c* columns are first differences and their lags.

formula: winperc ~ prerpi + postrpi_1 + (1 | team)
notes: Not used in the text; the help's notes ask whether the preseason RPI helps predict performance (such as win percentage or making the NCAA tournament) once the previous year's post-season RPI is controlled for, by multiple regression, with probit or logit for the tournament indicator (row 2), and say coaching experience can be added. Teams repeat over seasons, rendered as a team random intercept per this pass's panel ruling. wins and losses give winperc; postrpi is this season's post-season rank, an outcome; conference, power5, recruitrank, postrpi_2 and coachexper are unused; year is the season.

formula: tourney ~ prerpi + postrpi_1 + (1 | team)
notes: Row 1's reading with the tournament indicator as response; the help's notes name probit or logit for it, so the logit of the contract's rule stands.

formula: pctstck ~ choice + prftshr + female + age + educ + finc25 + finc35 + finc50 + finc75 + finc100 + finc101 + wealth89 + stckin89 + irain89 + (1 | id)
notes: Wooldridge page 506 (a chapter 14 computer exercise, recalled, not checked): some rows are spouses of one family (id), a cluster sample with clusters of at most two; pctstck is regressed by OLS on these regressors ignoring the clustering, then with cluster-robust errors and family fixed effects (Papke 2004, National Longitudinal Survey of Mature Women). Rendered per this pass's panel ruling with a family random intercept. pctstck holds three ordered codes (0 mostly bonds, 50 mixed, 100 mostly stocks) fitted as linear, hence gaussian. pyears, married and black are unused.

formula: lcriv ~ lpris + log(polpc) + log(incpc) + unem + black + metro + ag0_14 + ag15_17 + ag18_24 + ag25_34 + factor(year) + (1 | state)
notes: Wooldridge pages 573-574 (a chapter 16 computer exercise after Levitt 1996, recalled, not checked): the change in log violent crime gcriv on gpris and the changes of the controls (gpolpc, gincpc, cunem, cblack, cmetro, the age shares) with year dummies, by OLS on the first differences and then with final1 and final2 instrumenting gpris; no random-effects fit. Rendered in levels per this pass's panel ruling with a state random intercept (50 states and DC, 1980-1993). crip and its forms are the property-crime alternate response; criv and pris are the raw forms of lcriv and lpris; y81-y93 code year; govelec, final1 and final2 are unused.

formula: lrent ~ y90 + lpop + lavginc + pctstu + (1 | city)
notes: Wooldridge pages 160, 477 and 503-504 (computer exercises, recalled, not checked): log(rent) on y90, log(pop), log(avginc) and pctstu, pooled over 1980 and 1990 by OLS, then first differences and fixed effects; rendered per this pass's panel ruling with a city random intercept (64 college towns). The help's notes also sketch housing demand and supply equations for ltothsg with pctstu as instrument (ltothsg and lrnthsg are alternate responses). The c* columns are 1980-1990 changes; rent, pop and avginc are the raw forms of the logs; year aliases y90; lenroll is log(enroll).

formula: math4 ~ lavgrexpp + lunch + lenrol + factor(year) + (1 | schid)
notes: The help's notes: school-level data of Papke (2005), unbalanced; the usual RE and FE methods apply directly, and Computer Exercise 17 of chapter 14 walks through the correlated random effects version of the Hausman test (Wooldridge page 491). The regressors are recalled from Papke's model (math4 on the log of real spending averaged over the current and previous year, lunch, log enrollment and year effects), not checked. distid, the school's district, is a higher level not fitted; y93-y98 code year; exppp, rexpp and lrexpp are other spending forms and enrol the raw enrollment; found is unused.

formula: voteA ~ lexpendA + lexpendB + prtystrA + (1 | state)
notes: Wooldridge pages 34-39 and 164 (Example 2.5 regresses voteA on shareA; a chapter 4 exercise, recalled, regresses voteA on log(expendA), log(expendB) and prtystrA), OLS on 173 two-candidate 1988 House races. Races repeat within states, rendered as a state random intercept per the repeating-cluster ruling though the source treats them as independent. district numbers races within a state; expendA and expendB are the raw spending and shareA the derived spending share; democA is unused.

formula: lwage ~ educ + black + hisp + exper + I(exper^2) + married + union + factor(year) + (1 | nr)
notes: Wooldridge Example 14.4 (pages 494-495, Table 14.2; recalled): the wage equation for 545 men 1980-1987 (Vella and Verbeek 1998) by pooled OLS, random effects and fixed effects on educ, black, hisp, exper, exper squared, married, union and year dummies; linearmodels' panel example (bashtage.github.io/linearmodels/panel/examples/examples.html) fits RandomEffects of lwage on black, hisp, exper, expersq, married, educ, union and year on this table. Pages 480 and 505 are exercises on the same data. expersq is exper squared; d81-d87 code year; the industry, occupation, region, hours and poorhlth columns are unused. Same data as plm Males and rabe_hesketh wagepan.dta.
